commands.command: good catch, and it was right — the loopback gate has been removed rather than patched. verified the counterexample before acting: `ssh -n -l 18789:127.0.0.1:18789` is the documented default in seven docs pages, and `docs/platforms/mac/remote.md` says so explicitly ("the gateway sees the node's ip as `127.0.0.1` because the tunnel is loopback"). server-side peer ip is fooled the same way, so a browser genuinely cannot distinguish a local gateway from a tunneled one. rather than add provenance to the protocol, the fix uses a signal the native macos app already publishes: `appstate.connectionmode` (`local`/`remote`) is serialised as `kind` on each entry of `window.__openclaw_native_gateways__` by `dashboardgatewaycatalog`, so a tunneled gateway is `"remote"` despite its loopback url. the gate reads that through the existing `nativegatewayscapability` seam. consequence, stated plainly: the editor handoff is now native-app-only. a plain browser never offers it, including at genuine `localhost` on linux and windows. that is a deliberate owner decision — no authoritative locality signal exists in a browser, and a dead menu item is worse than none. test coverage now includes the tunnel case (native `kind: "remote"`), and the guards are verified to fail when the predicate is forced back to "always local". pr body and screenshots have been rewritten; the earlier loopback-era screenshots no longer describe shipped behavior.
